name: Umm Jirsan lava tube
region: Harrat Khaybar ~125 km N of Madinah
key_facts: Longest reported lava tube in Arabia: 1481 m; passages 8-12 m high, up to 45 m wide; three segments split by two roof collapses
access_note: Main collapse entrance walled with a staircase since 2017

name: Umm Jirsan east collapse (Area D)
key_facts: Second collapse entrance on the eastern passage
access_note: Inside same lava field as Umm Jirsan

name: Collapsed lava tube with rock art
region: Harrat Khaybar 1.3 km E of Umm Jirsan
key_facts: Large collapse entrance; sediment reaches ceiling after ~75 m; 16 rock-art panels

name: Harrat Khaybar (summit area)
region: NW Saudi Arabia N of Madinah
key_facts: Basaltic field built over ~5 million years; summit 2093 m; cones incl. Jabal Abyad and Jabal Bayda
access_note: Large field; roads reach oasis edges

name: Al Wahbah crater
key_facts: ~2 km wide, ~250 m deep; white salt-crust floor; steep walls
access_note: About 2 h drive from Taif airport via highway and paved roads

name: Harrat Rahat
key_facts: Largest lava field in Saudi Arabia (~20,000 km2); 900+ vents in the north; last eruption 1256 CE

name: Wabar impact craters
analog_for: True impact site / dust and dunes
key_facts: Confirmed impact craters; largest ~116 m; impact glass; meteorite fragments
access_note: Deep desert - hardest access on the list

name: Harrat Uwayrid
key_facts: ~7150 km2 basalt plateau with younger cinder cones; up to 1920 m

name: Ghar Al Hibashi lava tube
region: Harrat Nawasif/Al Buqum ~245 km SE of Makkah
key_facts: Surveyed lava tube (length reported as 689.5 m and 581 m in different sources); richest cave-mineral site in Saudi Arabia
